newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's KCRC assessing J-Fleming pension management.
newsitem.headline: HK's KCRC assessing J-Fleming pension management.

text.p: Hong Kong's Kowloon-Canton Railway Corp (KCRC) said on Tuesday Jardine Fleming Investment Management's continued management of a portion of the rail operator's pension fund was being assessed by its legal advisers and pension fund consultants.

"Following the case of the Hong Kong Jockey Club, we are now working with the benefit scheme consultants and our legal advisers to assess the situation," Michelle Leung, of KCRC's public affairs department, said by telephone.
Asked whether KCRC has placed Jardine Fleming's management mandate under review, Leung replied: "Yes".
Jardine Fleming executives were not immediately available for comment.
On October 3, the Hong Kong Jockey Club confirmed it had withdrawn HK$1 billion invested with Jardine Fleming after a recent fund management trading scandal.
The chief investment officer at Jardine Fleming Investment Management was allocating trades late, prompting heavy penalties from regulators in Hong Kong and London.
Jardine Fleming is a joint venture between Robert Fleming of London and Hong Kong-based Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd.
Leung said the KCRC performs a quarterly review of its fund managers and had asked Jardine Fleming for an explanation of the Jockey Club withdrawal at the regular review in September.

"It was a just a coincidence that in September it was our last review and we read the news from the media that the Hong Kong Jockey Club had withdrawn funds," Leung said. "We asked them to present their case."
The KCRC, a government-owned but privately managed body, declined to reveal the total value of its pension fund, but said contributions in 1995 totalled HK$85 million.
